tagline: Two of the four first towns, out to the salt marsh.
intro: A loop of 21 miles joins Exeter and Hampton, two of New Hampshire's four original towns, to Kensington and Hampton Falls, which were later cut out of them. The roads run between fields and woodland, out past the salt marshes, with views to the Atlantic.

Exeter was founded in 1638 by John Wheelwright, a clergyman exiled from Massachusetts. When the royal governor banned the rebel Provincial Congress from Portsmouth, it met in Exeter instead, and the town held the capital for 14 years.

moments.title: American Independence Museum
moments.text: A Dunlap broadside of the Declaration turned up in the attic of the Gilman family's Exeter house, and the museum built around it also keeps one of three original Purple Hearts.

moments.title: Kensington
moments.text: Of the 27 towns Governor Belcher granted, he gave names to only three, and this one he called after the owner of Kensington Palace.

moments.title: Hampton Falls
moments.text: Nearly a thousand acres of the Seabrook-Hamptons salt marsh lie in this one small town, drained by the Hampton Falls and Taylor rivers.
